Okay, so that means the micro-stutters aren\u0027t from that mod, but entirely because your computer is choking on that 19.3 GB RAM requirement. \n\nTo answer your question: **No, unfortunately, playing multiplayer will not fix this, and it might actually make it worse.** \n\nHere is why offloading to a server doesn\u0027t solve a RAM issue in tModLoader:\n\n**1. If you host the server on your own PC (Host \u0026 Play)**\nIf you try to play multiplayer by hosting it on your own computer, your PC now has to run the client (the game you are looking at) *and* the server (the background logic) at the same time. This actually requires **more** RAM and CPU power than playing single-player. \n\n**2. If you use a separate Dedicated Server (Paid host or a friend\u0027s PC)**\nEven if you offload the server to a completely different computer in another country, it won\u0027t fix your RAM issue. Here is why:\n*   **What the server handles:** AI, boss logic, world generation, and syncing players. \n*   **What YOUR PC still has to handle:** Every single texture, sprite, sound effect, music track, and weapon animation in the game. \n\nIn modded Terraria, the vast majority of memory is eaten up by **assets** (the pictures and sounds). Even if a server is doing the math, your 16 GB PC still has to physically load every massive Infernum boss sprite, every Catalyst weapon texture, and all of Wrath of the Gods\u0027 visual effects into its memory just to draw them on your screen. \n\nBecause both the server and the client *must* have the exact same mods loaded to connect to each other, your PC will still try to pull 19.3 GB of RAM, and you will still get massive lag from your page file.\n\n**The Hard Truth**\nWhen it comes to tModLoader, there are only two ways past a memory bottleneck:\n1. **Reduce the amount of graphics/sounds being loaded** (by disabling Catalyst and WOTG until you beat Infernum, like the \"Endgame Swap\" strategy).\n2. **Buy more physical RAM** (Upgrading from 16 GB to 32 GB of RAM would instantly allow you to play all of these mods at the exact same time with zero issues). \n\nI know it\u0027s a bummer, but definitely try just playing Infernum + Calamity by themselves for now. The game will run so much smoother, and it will be a much better experience!",

      "text": "whaat exactly is calvalex?\n",
      "role": "user",
      "tokenCount": 10,
      "createTime": "2026-06-10T10:30:42.058Z"
    }, {
      "text": "**Defining the Calvalex Mod**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on defining CalValEX. It appears to be a mod, specifically, a mod for Terraria/tModLoader. The next step is fleshing out what specific content and mechanics it adds to that game.\n\n\n**Clarifying the Focus**\n\nI\u0027ve learned that \"CalValEX\" is actually short for \"Calamity\u0027s Vanities Extra\", and it\u0027s a cosmetic mod for Terraria. It adds many vanity items, including pets, mounts, furniture, and blocks, all based on the Calamity Mod. The memory issue boils down to the huge number of image assets, animations, and sound files necessary to support all those items.\n\n\n",
      "role": "model",
      "tokenCount": 580,
      "isThought": true,
      "parts": [{
        "text": "**Defining the Calvalex Mod**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on defining CalValEX. It appears to be a mod, specifically, a mod for Terraria/tModLoader. The next step is fleshing out what specific content and mechanics it adds to that game.\n\n\n",
        "thought": true
      }, {
        "text": "**Clarifying the Focus**\n\nI\u0027ve learned that \"CalValEX\" is actually short for \"Calamity\u0027s Vanities Extra\", and it\u0027s a cosmetic mod for Terraria. It adds many vanity items, including pets, mounts, furniture, and blocks, all based on the Calamity Mod. The memory issue boils down to the huge number of image assets, animations, and sound files necessary to support all those items.\n\n\n",
        "thought": true
      }],
      "createTime": "2026-06-10T10:30:42.058Z"
    }, {
      "text": "**CalValEX** stands for **\"Calamity\u0027s Vanities\"**. \n\nIt is a massive add-on mod for Calamity that is entirely focused on **cosmetics, building, and vanity items.** It does not add any new bosses, weapons, or progression to the game. \n\nInstead, it adds hundreds of visual-only items based on the Calamity universe, including:\n*   **Pets \u0026 Light Pets:** Over 80+ unique pets (mini versions of Calamity bosses and enemies).\n*   **Mounts:** Over 50+ new mounts.\n*   **Vanity Outfits:** Dozens of costumes and masks.\n*   **Furniture \u0026 Blocks:** Hundreds of new building materials, paintings, and boss-themed furniture sets.\n*   **Critters:** Harmless ambient creatures that spawn in the world.\n\n**Why it\u0027s causing problems for your PC:**\nEven though CalValEX doesn\u0027t change combat or gameplay, it is incredibly heavy on your RAM. Every single one of those pets has running, flying, and idle animations. Every piece of furniture has a texture. Your computer has to load thousands of these image files into its memory the moment you start tModLoader, just in case you decide to use one of them. \n\n**The Good News:**\nBecause it is 100% cosmetic, **disabling CalValEX will not affect your Infernum playthrough at all.** You won\u0027t miss out on any weapons, boss fights, or lore. \n\nIf you disable it, you will instantly free up a huge chunk of RAM because your PC won\u0027t have to load all those pet animations and furniture sprites! It is one of the easiest mods to turn off when you are trying to save your computer\u0027s memory.",

      "finishReason": "STOP",
      "tokenCount": 378,

      "text": "**Considering the User\u0027s Request**\n\nI\u0027m starting by carefully examining the user\u0027s request concerning the \"Infernal Eclipse of Ragnarok\" Terraria mod.       "text": "I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but if you try to load **Infernal Eclipse of Ragnarok** on your PC right now, your computer might actually explode. (Or, more realistically, tModLoader will just instantly crash). \n\nHere is why:\n\n\"Infernal Eclipse of Ragnarok\" isn\u0027t just a single mod; it is an **ultra-modded mega-pack**. It is specifically designed to combine almost every massive content mod in Terraria into one single playthrough. \n\nIf you look at the mod list for that pack, it forces you to run:\n*   **Calamity** AND **Infernum** AND **Catalyst** AND **Wrath of the Gods (Noxus)**...\n*   ...PLUS **Thorium** (Another massive, game-sized mod)\n*   ...PLUS **Secrets of the Shadows** (Huge content mod)\n*   ...PLUS **Consolaria**\n*   ...PLUS dozens of other expansion mods and quality-of-life add-ons.\n\n**The RAM Math:**\nRemember how your PC with 16 GB of RAM is already choking and freezing because your current mod list needs **19.3 GB**? \n\nIf you try to load the Infernal Eclipse modpack, it is going to try to pull something insane like **24 to 32 GB of RAM**. Your computer will immediately run out of memory, push everything to your storage drive, and your game will drop to about 1 frame per minute before completely crashing. \n\n**The Verdict:**\nTo play a mega-pack like Infernal Eclipse, **32 GB of physical RAM is an absolute minimum requirement.** \n\nKeep that modpack bookmarked! It is an amazing, crazy project, and it would be the perfect thing to play if you ever decide to buy a RAM upgrade for your PC. But for today, stick to your \"Mod Diet.\" Play just Calamity + Infernum so your 16 GB of RAM can actually breathe, and enjoy the smooth boss fights!",

      "parts": [{
        "text": "I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but if you try to load **Infernal Eclipse of Ragnarok"
      }, {
        "text": "** on your PC right now, your computer might actually explode. (Or, more realistically, tModLoader will just instantly"
      }, {
        "text": " crash). \n\nHere is why:\n\n\"Infernal Eclipse of Ragnarok\" isn\u0027t just a single mod; it is an **"
      }, {
        "text": "ultra-modded mega-pack**. It is specifically"
      }, {
        "text": " designed to combine almost every massive content mod in Terraria into one single playthrough. \n\nIf you look at the"
      }, {
        "text": " mod list for that pack, it forces you to run:\n*   **Calamity** AND **Infernum** AND"
      }, {
        "text": " **Catalyst** AND **Wrath of the Gods (Noxus)**..."
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   ...PLUS **Thorium** (Another massive, game-sized mod)"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   ...PLUS **Secrets of the Shadows** (Huge content mod)"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   ...PLUS **Consolaria**"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   ...PLUS dozens of other expansion mods and quality-of-life add"
      }, {
        "text": "-ons.\n\n**The RAM Math:**\nRemember how"
      }, {
        "text": " your PC with 16 GB of RAM is already choking and freezing because your current mod list needs **19.3 GB"
      }, {
        "text": "**? \n\nIf you try to load the Infernal Eclipse modpack, it is going to try to pull something"
      }, {
        "text": " insane like **24 to 32 GB of RAM**. Your computer will immediately run out of memory, push everything to your"
      }, {
        "text": " storage drive, and your game will drop to about 1 frame per minute before completely crashing. \n\n**The Verdict"
      }, {
        "text": ":**\nTo play a mega-pack like Infernal Eclipse, **32 GB of physical RAM is an absolute minimum requirement.** \n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "Keep that modpack bookmarked! It is an amazing, crazy project, and it would be the perfect thing to play if"
      }, {
        "text": " you ever decide to buy a RAM upgrade for your PC. But"
      }, {
        "text": " for today, stick to your \"Mod Diet.\" Play just Calamity + Infernum so your 16 GB of"
      }, {
        "text": " RAM can actually breathe, and enjoy the smooth boss fights!"
      }, {
        "text": "",
        "thoughtSignature": ""
      }],

      "text": "You hit the nail right on the head—adding **Calamity Overhaul** to your current setup is a *terrible* idea! :3\n\nEven if you had a supercomputer from NASA, I would still tell you not to use it right now. Here is why Calamity Overhaul is a trap for your specific playthrough:\n\n**1. It is the ultimate enemy of Infernum**\nInfernum is all about meticulously recoded, beautifully choreographed, and highly difficult boss AI. Calamity Overhaul, on the other hand, notoriously messes with boss priorities, weapon damage scaling, and game mechanics. \nIf you play them together, Calamity Overhaul often breaks Infernum\u0027s custom boss behaviors. Bosses might bug out, despawn, or completely break their attack patterns. The modding community highly recommends keeping Overhaul far, far away from Infernum!\n\n**2. The Performance Nightmare**\nCalamity Overhaul adds complex mechanics like manual reloading, new ammo types, and heavy visual effects for almost every weapon in the game. This means the mod is constantly running tons of complex math and calculations in the background while you shoot. \nIf your PC is already gasping for air trying to manage 19.3 GB of RAM, the background processing from Calamity Overhaul will likely tank your frames to the single digits the second you fire a weapon. \n\n**3. It\u0027s notoriously incompatible**\nIn the tModLoader community, Calamity Overhaul has a bit of a reputation for simply not playing nice with other large mods. It changes so many core aspects of Calamity that it causes visual glitches and multiplayer desyncs if you look at it funny.\n\n**The Verdict:**\nIf your goal is to experience the pure, cinematic boss fights of Infernum without your PC catching on fire, **do not install Calamity Overhaul.** \n\nStick to the pure Calamity + Infernum combo for the smoothest, most enjoyable (and least buggy!) experience!",
